newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- FEB 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- FEB 21.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
KATHIMERINI

--Greek shares overcame the 1,300 resistance level at yesterday's session on the Athens bourse, breaking a six-year record. Stocks have seen profits of 40 percent since the beginning of the year and the trend appears set to continue.
--Turnover in gambling in Greece reached 650 billion drachmas last year, an increase of 30 percent over the previous year. The increase is primarily due to the operation of more private casinos.

--The National Bank of Greece will unveil a new investment product at its press conference today. Sources said Governor Theodoros Karatzas will reveal a 3-4 year investment loan with a variable interest rate, close to that for three-year bonds.
--There's uncertainty over the agreement for the sale of Cambas Wines following a disagreement between the National Bank and Citibank Leasing.
IMERISIA
--Banks once again led the assault on the 1,300 mark at the bourse yesterday. Banks have gained 50.56 percent since the beginning of the year.
--The current accounts deficit widened in January-October 1996 by 41 percent, totalling 4.3 billlion dollars and causing concern amongst officials.
--OTE, Greece's telecommunications organisation, yesterday gave notice it would unveil its new mobile phone next September.
KERDOS

--Rescheduling debts by hotels were discussed yesterday by hoteliers and National Bank of Greece Governor Theodoros Karatzas. Karatzas was sympathetic to the difficulty in repayments caused by high interest rates but said he could not intervene with banks.
--The government will turn to the private sector to fill the gaps in financing needed for major public projects such as the Egnatia highway and the bridge over the Maliakou Gulf.
EXPRESS
--High foreign exchange deposits in the country of over 20 billion dollars and its negative effect on the current account deficit is worrying the Bank of Greece.
--The government will make its final decision on the fate of OTE's second float by the end of the month: up to 17 percent of the company can be offered.
--Greeks may not be setting their clocks back next month if the government accepts a proposal to harmonise times across Europe and allow markets in the European Union to operate at the same time.
NAFTEMBORIKI
--The finance ministry is putting the final touches to a bill defining more reasonable and effective fines and penalties for tax evasion.

--The National Bank is expected to lead the charge on breaking the 10.0 barrier in interest rates. Sources say interest on deposit accounts will fall to 9.5 percent while rates for housing loans will also fall. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
